goal: Teach frontend-oriented AEM developers how content policies govern component capability by template context, how Allowed Components and policy defaults shape authoring, and how the Style System connects semantic author choices to deployed CSS.

deck_context.source_summary: Class 7 of a seven-week AEM Sites course, delivered Tuesday, August 25, 2026. The audience understands JCR Resources, Sling request resolution and editable-template structure versus initial content. This class completes the technical foundation for the individual Week 2 Guide Page authoring practice.
deck_context.core_claim: A safe AEM authoring contract combines reusable component code with narrowly scoped content policies, explicit container permissions and a small set of semantic styles whose CSS is deployed and tested.
canonical_facts: Component code defines technical capability; a content policy configures capability for a template context.
Policy mappings for editable-template component locations are stored below /conf/<site>/settings/wcm/templates/<template>/policies/jcr:content.
The cq:policy property holds a relative reference to a policy definition below /conf/<site>/settings/wcm/policies.
A layout container policy determines which components authors may insert in that container.
Policy defaults configure a reusable context; dialog values are authored on individual component instances below /content.
The Style System maps author-facing style names to CSS classes configured in a content policy.
Developers implement style classes in deployed client libraries; AEM applies selected classes to the component decoration wrapper.

slides.title: Govern authoring choices without changing component code.
slides.intent: Frame policies as the layer that turns reusable components into a controlled authoring experience.
key_points: Class 7 · Week 2 · Day 7 · August 25, 2026
Content policies, Allowed Components and Style System
Component capability → content policy → author choice
Juan Maldonado

layout.composition: Editorial technical cover with one central three-layer control diagram and exact class metadata aligned below the title.
layout.intent: Introduce the complete capability-to-choice chain without repeating the sample's repository trace.

constraints: Render all class metadata exactly.
Do not imply that content authors modify component code.

slides.title: A policy configures capability by context.
slides.intent: Separate technical component capability from the configuration permitted in one template location.
key_points: Component code defines what is technically possible
Content policy configures what is available in one template context
The same component can use different policies in different locations
Authors use the resulting choices without editing code
A shared policy change can affect every referencing location

local_context.required_background: Use one Image component implementation feeding a Guide Page context and an Article Page context. The Guide policy exposes a narrower choice set; the Article policy exposes a different set. Keep the implementation identical.

layout.composition: One component capability block branches into two contrasting template contexts, each with its own policy and author-facing results.
layout.intent: Use controlled branching to make context-specific configuration unmistakable.

visual_elements.main_visual: One implementation, two policies, two authoring outcomes.

constraints: Render the eyebrow exactly as '02 · POLICY CONTEXT'.
Label implementation, policy and author choice separately.
Do not show duplicated component code.
State that shared policy changes can have multiple consumers.

slides.title: Follow the policy mapping before editing code.
slides.intent: Make policy resolution concrete enough to diagnose a missing or unexpectedly configured component.
key_points: Start at the component path in the editable template
Find the matching node under policies/jcr:content
Read cq:policy and follow its relative reference
Inspect the resolved definition below /conf/wknd/settings/wcm/policies
Verify the mapping before changing rendering code

slides.title: Allowed Components belongs to the container policy.
slides.intent: Explain why an installed component may still be unavailable in the component browser.
key_points: Container policy controls which components authors may insert
Installed does not mean allowed in this container
Expose a small purpose-specific set
Missing selector entry usually points to policy or mapping
Validate one allowed and one disallowed state

constraints: Render the eyebrow exactly as '04 · ALLOWED COMPONENTS'.

slides.title: Policy defaults are not authored instance values.
slides.intent: Distinguish reusable design configuration from content stored on an individual component instance.
key_points: Policy defaults configure a reusable template context
Authored dialog values belong to one component instance
Policy configuration lives under /conf
Instance content lives under /content
Check policy reuse before changing a shared default

local_context.required_background: Compare an Image policy under /conf that permits widths and enables lazy loading with one Image component instance under /content that stores fileReference and alt text. Do not claim every Core Image property is necessarily a policy property; present these as representative categories.

layout.composition: Mirrored two-column repository inspectors with a narrow center divider labeled reusable context versus one authored instance; a reuse-impact callout spans the bottom.
layout.intent: Use repository ownership and scope to prevent configuration/content confusion.

visual_elements.main_visual: Policy values under /conf contrasted with authored values under /content.

constraints: Render the eyebrow exactly as '05 · DEFAULTS VS VALUES'.
Render /conf and /content exactly.

slides.title: Style System maps semantic choices to deployed CSS.
slides.intent: Show every dependency between an author-facing style name and the rendered result.
key_points: Template author maps Style Name to CSS Classes in policy
Featured → cmp-guide--featured
Developer implements the class in a deployed client library
Content author selects the style in Page Editor
AEM applies the class to the component decoration wrapper

local_context.required_background: The Style System exposes a user-friendly Style Name while CSS class names remain implementation-oriented. CSS and optional JavaScript must already be deployed. The selected class is applied to the component decoration wrapper; Style System does not generate CSS.

layout.composition: A five-stage horizontal pipeline with distinct owner labels above each step and an exact class token flowing through to a simplified DOM wrapper at the end.
layout.intent: Make ownership and implementation dependencies visible in the order they execute.

visual_elements.main_visual: Style Name → policy mapping → client library → author selection → wrapper class.

constraints: Render the eyebrow exactly as '06 · STYLE SYSTEM'.

slides.title: Key takeaways
slides.intent: Retrieve the five distinctions developers need before completing the Guide Page practice.
key_points: Component code defines capability; policy configures it by context
cq:policy connects template location to policy definition
Container policy controls Allowed Components
Policy defaults differ from authored instance values
Semantic style choices require deployed, tested CSS
